title: Spacing and Retrieval Retention Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Predict which review schedule and method keep the most memory for a day-30 exam, then compare forgetting curves for massed, spaced, and expanding reviews.

learningObjectives: The learner will compare predicted retention under massed, evenly spaced, and expanding review schedules, each done by rereading or by retrieval, and correctly predict which schedule and method retain the most on a day-30 exam.
prerequisites: Learning versus performance, forgetting curve, spaced practice, massed practice, retrieval practice, and desirable difficulty, from Chapter 1.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit a prediction, then compare model curves
keyQuestions: Which schedule keeps the most memory on day 30?
Why does cramming win on day 1?
commonMisconceptions: Cramming is efficient because it gives the best score on tomorrow's test
Rereading is as good as testing yourself
The total time spent studying is what matters, not when it happens
assessmentOpportunities: Which schedule and method give the highest day-30 retention?
Why does massed review win on day 1 but fail on day 30?
Why can equal study time give different results?

controls.name: P1 and P2 buttons
controls.description: Choose a schedule and a method as predictions, then press Submit predictions.

controls.name: Review method
controls.description: Switch between Reread and Retrieval after the predictions.

controls.name: Exam day
controls.description: Switch the exam to day 1, 7, or 30.

controls.name: P3 buttons and Check P3
controls.description: Choose and check the best schedule for a day-1 exam.

controls.name: Reset
controls.description: Returns to the opening state with no curves.
